    "summary": "[GOAL] Redaction is display-only: bash argv byte-identical under redaction, single-token [REDACTED:*] markers, --dart-define carve-out from the entropy layer — placeholder never reaches a child process",
    "description": "**[GOAL] Redaction is a mask over what is SEEN, never a rewrite of what is EXECUTED: bash argv stays byte-identical under redaction, placeholders are single tokens, and ordinary `--dart-define` values are not secrets**

*(v2 — reformatted per the repo's GOAL discipline; original report preserved verbatim at the bottom. Severity: HIGH — the redactor corrupts executable commands; a passing-looking test command silently tests the wrong build.)*

## Goal — display-only redaction (v2)
One sentence: **turning redaction on never changes what a child process receives: argv is byte-identical, transcripts show masks, and the entropy layer stops classifying ordinary compile-time defines as secrets.**

## Pinned facts (incident + code)
- The executed command carried the literal `[REDACTED:High Entropy String]` — with SPACES — split by the shell into 3 argv items (`[REDACTED:High`, `Entropy`, `String]`), which the Flutter test loader tried to open as paths. So a redacted string flowed into EXECUTION, not just display.
- Trigger: the entropy layer (L9, `lib/src/redact/layer_entropy.dart`) matches high-Shannon-entropy ASCII tokens ≥ minLength — `JSR_THREE_EXAMPLE=webgl_geometry_colors` style define values qualify. The shell-split workaround (assigning to env vars first) proves the pattern match on the RAW command string is the gate.
- Prime suspect for the execution rewrite: `lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart` (imported by `builtin_tools.dart` for the bash path) — the approval-layer shape redactor must be audited first; also audit persisted-call replay and any other site where a redacted string can flow into argv. Implementation step 1 = pin the exact rewrite site with a failing argv-equality test.

## Invariants to pin
- **I1 — Display-only:** with redaction ON vs OFF, the argv received by the executor is byte-identical for any command containing non-secret values (property test over a corpus incl. defines, paths, URLs, base64 fragments).
- **I2 — Single-token markers:** every `[REDACTED:<kind>]` marker contains no whitespace — anywhere it CAN leak into a shell string it stays one argv item. (Even after I1, defense in depth.)
- **I3 — Defines are not secrets by default:** `--dart-define=K=V`, `-DK=V`, and env-style `K=V` assignments in bash commands are exempt from the entropy layer; REGISTERED secrets still match (registered layer outranks carve-outs; blockMode/deny behavior for credentials unchanged).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — The exact repro command executes with original argv (fake-shell capture asserts byte-equality) while the persisted transcript shows the masked form — both properties in one test.
- **AC2** — Single-token marker invariant: UT over all layer markers (render with whitespace-free assertion; fix the label rendering if any marker can embed spaces).
- **AC3** — Defines carve-out: entropy layer does not match `--dart-define=K=V` / `-DK=V` / `K=V` shapes (UT: representative corpus incl. uppercase-snake values stays clean; embedded REAL entropy-class secrets inside defines still match).
- **AC4** — REG: credential paths, PEM blobs, tokens with vendor/context context are still masked in display paths and still denied in blockMode — the carve-out opens no hole (shared redaction suites stay green; red REG blocks merge).
- **AC5** — Site audit: every site that can feed a redacted string into execution (bash_shape_redaction, persisted-call replay, steering rewrites) carries an argv-preservation property test or a comment-verified impossibility.

## Edge / border cases
A define value that IS a registered secret (registered match wins: mask display; execution per blockMode policy — if blocked, the error names the define); define values containing spaces/quotes (shell-safe both masked and raw); Windows `cmd /c` path; long option spellings from the bash guard's residual-caveat list; entropy threshold unchanged for non-define contexts.

## Non-goals
No global entropy-threshold changes; no removal of the entropy layer; no changes to RESULT masking (afterToolCall/persist display masking is correct as-is); no new config surface (carve-outs are shape-based, not configurable lists).

## References
Original report below; `lib/src/redact/layer_entropy.dart` (L9), `lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart` bash path; issue #24 (redaction layering); `docs/redaction.md`.

The bash-tool secret redactor rewrites a non-secret `--dart-define` argument into the literal placeholder `[REDACTED:High Entropy String]`. This is not just transcript masking: the placeholder reaches the child process, and its spaces split it into multiple arguments.

Run through the `bash` tool:

flutter test test/three_example_selection_test.dart [REDACTED:High Entropy String]

Observed test-loader errors include attempts to load paths named:

```text
[REDACTED:High
Entropy
String]
```

A `flutter run` command with the same define also receives the damaged argument; the compiled default is used instead of the requested example. Process inspection shows the literal placeholder in the launched Flutter tool command.

Split the same non-secret value in shell so the raw tool command does not match the redaction pattern:

```sh
DEF='JSR_THREE_EXAMPLE'
EXAMPLE='webgl_geometry_colors'
flutter test test/three_example_selection_test.dart --dart-define="${DEF}=${EXAMPLE}"
```

This reaches Flutter correctly and the selection test passes.

## Expected

Redaction must not rewrite ordinary Dart compile-time defines. If a value truly must be redacted, preserve it as one argv item and never inject whitespace into executable commands; transcript masking should not alter process semantics."

content.text:
# Secret redaction (layered pipeline)

Layered detection + masking of secret-shaped content in everything that
flows through the agent — tool results, the provider context, and user
prompts — so secrets never reach the LLM, the transcript, or the session
JSONL (issue #24).

Two systems run side by side:

- The **legacy exact-value `SecretRedactor`** masks values it was told
  about by name (provider API keys, `request_secret` grants). Attached
  lazily on runtime tokens (CLI) or at construction (app).
- The **layered `RedactionPipeline`** catches secret-shaped content it was
  never told about: vendor tokens, PEM/ASN.1 blobs, credential-file paths
  and whole-file dumps, connection strings, high-entropy strings,
  private-key contexts. Attach point: `attachRedactionPipeline`.

## Layers

Priority order (higher wins overlaps): `registered` (exact values) →
`path` (credential files) → `credential` (DOM form-field values) →
`vendor` (GitHub/AWS/OpenAI/JWT/…) → `prefix` (`indexOf` pre-screen
feeding vendor) → `pem` → `asn1` → `connection` → `context`
(password/secret key names) → `entropy` → `pii` (off by
default). Output markers are `[REDACTED:<kind>]`, idempotent, and
line-count preserving. Allowlisted shapes (Git SHAs, UUIDs) and
`data:` base64 URLs survive.

## Config (`redact:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project `.fah/config.yaml`)

```yaml
redact:
  enabled: true        # master switch (default true)
  blockMode: false     # ALSO deny read/bash touching credential files
  layers:
    pii: true          # per-layer overrides
    entropy: false
  allowlist:           # regexes whose full match suppress redaction
    - '[0-9a-f]{40}'
  toolAllow: [read]    # hook-level policy: only these tools get redacted
  toolDeny: [write]    # never redacted (wins over toolAllow)
```

Defaults are never written back to the config file. `enabled: false`
keeps the pipeline unattached entirely.

## Semantics

- **Session safety (AC1)**: tool results are masked by the
  `afterToolCall` hook BEFORE they are persisted — the JSONL never sees
  the raw secret.
- **Write-side exclusion (AC7)**: `write`, `edit`, `checkpoint`, and MCP
  write-ish tool outputs are NEVER redacted — that text is code the model
  produced; key-shaped strings in it are the deliverable. An exception to
  the exclusion stays an exception.
- **blockMode (AC6)**: `read`/`bash` calls that would touch a credential
  file (`.env`, `[REDACTED:Credential File]`, `[REDACTED:Credential File]`, `[REDACTED:Credential File]`, `[REDACTED:Credential File]`,
  `[REDACTED:Credential File]`, `.pem`/`.key`) are denied with a human reason.
  Mask mode (default) only masks the result.
- **Prompt entry (AC8)**: user prompt text is masked before it reaches
  the agent/session (`redactPrompt`, counted under `user_input`).
- **Registered secrets**: every value registered into the legacy
  redactor (catalog keys, role secrets, keychain preload, `/provider`
  tokens, `request_secret` grants) also feeds the pipeline's
  `registered` layer.

## CLI

`/redact` — status (on/off, blockMode, registered secret count, session
match count). Subcommands: `on|off`, `block on|off`, `stats` (matches per
layer and per tool), `layers` (per-layer toggle state).

arguments.newText:
Priority order (higher wins overlaps): `registered` (exact values) →
`path` (credential files) → `credential` (DOM form-field values) →
`vendor` (GitHub/AWS/OpenAI/JWT/…) → `prefix` (`indexOf` pre-screen
feeding vendor) → `pem` → `asn1` → `connection` → `context`
(password/secret key names) → `entropy` → `pii` (off by
default). Output markers are `[REDACTED:<kind>]`, idempotent, and
line-count preserving. Allowlisted shapes (Git SHAs, UUIDs) and
`data:` base64 URLs survive.

Markers are single shell tokens (gh-1952): every whitespace run in a
kind label renders as `-` (`[REDACTED:GitHub-Token]`), so a marker that
leaks into a shell string can never split into several argv items.

## Redaction is display-only (gh-1952)

Turning redaction on never changes what a child process receives: the
`bash` tool's argv is byte-identical with redaction ON vs OFF for every
non-secret value. The only execution rewrite is the approval-layer
shape interceptor (issue #1408), bounded to recognized vendor token
shapes — ordinary compile-time defines (`--dart-define=K=V`, `-DK=V`,
env-style `K=V` assignments) are exempt from the entropy heuristic
altogether; registered and vendor-shaped secrets still match inside
defines (the carve-out never outranks a real layer).

+/// gh-1952 (I3): compile-time defines and env-style assignments are not
+/// secrets by default. The token charset includes `=` and `-`, so a
+/// whole define argument is ONE candidate token — the incident command's

+/// reached the child process. These shapes are exempt from THIS

+/// context, ...) outrank the entropy layer and still match inside
+/// defines.
+final RegExp _dartDefineFlag = RegExp(r'^--dart-define=');
+final RegExp _dartDefineShortFlag = RegExp(r'^-D[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*=');
+final RegExp _envAssignment = RegExp(r'^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*=');

+/// `-DK=V`) or an env-style `K=V` assignment. Quoted define values

+/// carry the `K=V` assignment shape. Shape-based, not configurable
+/// (gh-1952 non-goals).
+bool _isDefineOrAssignmentToken(String token) =>
+    _dartDefineFlag.hasMatch(token) ||

arguments.content:
### What changed
Redaction is now display-only at the bash path: a non-secret command reaches the child process byte-identical with redaction ON vs OFF, every `[REDACTED:<kind>]` marker renders as a single shell token, and ordinary compile-time defines are exempt from the entropy heuristic.

### Key decisions
- `redactionMarker` (the ONE marker construction site, now shared by the pipeline, the #1408 bash shape rewriter and the wire protocol's `redactForLog`) normalizes whitespace runs to `-`: `[REDACTED:GitHub-Token]`, `[REDACTED:High-Entropy-String]` — a marker that leaks into a shell string can no longer split into 3 argv items like the incident's spaced marker did (I2). Labels themselves keep their human-readable form for notices/stats; the pipeline's marker-skip regex is label-agnostic so old transcripts stay idempotent.
- Entropy carve-out (I3, shape-based, not configurable): tokens reading as `--dart-define=K=V`, `-DK=V`, `--dart-define "K=V"` (quoted or space form, dotted keys) or env-style `K=V` assignments are exempt from the entropy layer only — registered/vendor/PEM/context layers outrank the carve-out and still match inside defines (a `ghp_…` define value still rewrites and the notice still names it).
- Site audit (AC5): the shape interceptor remains the only execution-feed seam (foreground, yield-aware job and background paths all share `_rewriteShellCommand`); persisted-call replay and steering rewrites are comment-verified impossibilities (records reload as context only; soft-yield hands the SAME process to a background job). Argv-equality property tests pin the bash path end-to-end.
- Marker literals across ~75 fixtures/docs aligned to the single-token rendering (mechanical).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/redact/ test/approval/bash_shape_redaction_test.dart
dart test --tags integration test/integration/redaction_e2e_test.dart
```
The gh-1952 e2e pins AC1 in one test: the exact repro define command executes with original argv (fake-shell capture, byte-equality) while the persisted session record shows the registered-secret variant masked.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CALL[bash tool call] --> RW[_rewriteShellCommand — vendor shapes only]
  RW -->|non-secret define| EXEC[env.exec — byte-identical argv]
  RW -->|vendor-shaped secret| MK[redactionMarker — single token] --> EXEC
  EXEC --> RES[tool result] --> PIPE[RedactionPipeline afterToolCall] --> JSONL[session JSONL: masked display]
  DEF[--dart-define=K=V] -.->|entropy carve-out| PASS[stays clean everywhere]
```

</details>

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  SHARED FAST GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL   ║

# ║  duplication < 1% (flutter_app < 3.7%) · cross-module < 0.31%             ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# THE shared fast gate used by BOTH the pre-commit hook and CI (issue #177,
# AC7). Both callers run this exact script and diff the one-line markers
#   GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>
# for hook/CI parity. Every known stage ALWAYS prints exactly one marker:
# OK when it ran and passed, SKIP <reason> when it was not selected or a
# required tool is missing. A failing stage aborts the script with exit 1
# BEFORE its OK marker is printed (marker absent = failed).
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh [--scope auto|all|core|app|docs] [--stages list] [--hook]
#
#   --scope auto  Derive the scope from changed paths (default):
#                 - in a git hook (--hook flag or GIT_INDEX_FILE set):
#                   staged files via `git diff --cached --name-only`;
#                 - in CI (BASE_REF + HEAD_REF env vars set):
#                   `git diff --name-only $BASE_REF...$HEAD_REF`;
#                 - otherwise: "all" (safe default).
#   --scope all   Run every stage.
#   --scope core  analyze + test-core + coverage + crap + dup + dupx.
#   --scope app   analyze + dup + dupx + flutter.
#   --scope docs  analyze only.
#   --stages l    Comma-separated stage list; overrides the scope-derived set.
#                 Known stages: analyze,test-core,coverage,crap,dup,dupx,flutter,integration-mock
#
#
# Path rules (union logic, E1; test/** counts as core, E6):
#   docs/ | *.md | prompts/ .................. analyze
#   lib/ | bin/ | test/ | pubspec.* .......... + test-core, coverage, crap, dup, dupx
#   test/integration/** ...................... + integration-mock (no-key legs,
#                                              MockLlmServer; issue #551)
#   flutter_app/ | packages/ ................. + dup, dupx, flutter
#   scripts/ | .github/ | crap4dart.yaml ..... ALL stages (safe default, E2)
#   anything unknown ......................... ALL stages (safe default)
#

# load-sensitive PTY/grid timing legs stop costing a full 2.5 h leg per
# ambient flake (default 0 = single-shot, behaviour unchanged).
#

# lib/bin files only — the ratchet guards what a commit touches, so a
# pre-existing offender in an untouched file cannot block an unrelated
# commit. Non-hook runs (and ci.yml's whole-repo `crap4dart analyze`)
# keep the full-repo view, so nothing escapes the ratchet permanently.

content.text:
+Markers are single shell tokens (gh-1952): every whitespace run in a
+kind label renders as `-` (`[REDACTED:GitHub-Token]`), so a marker that
+leaks into a shell string can never split into several argv items.
+
+## Redaction is display-only (gh-1952)
+
+Turning redaction on never changes what a child process receives: the
+`bash` tool's argv is byte-identical with redaction ON vs OFF for every
+non-secret value. The only execution rewrite is the approval-layer
+shape interceptor (issue #1408), bounded to recognized vendor token
+shapes — ordinary compile-time defines (`--dart-define=K=V`, `-DK=V`,
+env-style `K=V` assignments) are exempt from the entropy heuristic
+altogether; registered and vendor-shaped secrets still match inside
+defines (the carve-out never outranks a real layer).
+
